ra: The Horned God is a core deity of the Wiccan pantheon hub.
The Triple Goddess is the principal female deity of the Wiccan pantheon hub.
The Dryghtyn / 'the One' belongs to the Wiccan theological collective as its ultimate principle.
The quarter-guardians are part of the Wiccan ritual-cosmological roster collected under the hub.
The Wheel of the Year is the central ritual cycle of the tradition grouped under the hub.
In Wiccan theology the God and Goddess emanate from the impersonal Dryghtyn / the One.
The Goddess is understood within the tradition as a manifestation emanating from the supreme Dryghtyn.
Wiccan duotheism pairs the Horned God and the Goddess as divine consorts whose union drives the seasonal cycle.
The sabbats of the Wheel of the Year dramatize the birth, life, death and rebirth of the Horned God.
The Wheel of the Year tracks the Goddess through her Maiden/Mother/Crone aspects across the seasons.
The Guardians of the Watchtowers are invoked to ward and protect the cast ritual circle in which the deities are worshipped.
Gardner and Valiente explicitly drew the Wiccan Horned God's imagery and name from the antlered Gaulish god Cernunnos (Hutton, Triumph of the Moon).
The Horned God's goat-horned, ithyphallic nature-deity persona derives from the 19th-century Romantic revival of the Greek Pan that fed directly into Wicca (Hutton).
The Crone aspect of the Wiccan Triple Goddess is identified with the classical lunar/chthonic Hecate.
The Maiden/huntress aspect of the Triple Goddess aligns with Diana, central to the Romantic 'Dianic' witch-cult lineage absorbed by Wicca.
The lunar Mother aspect of the Triple Goddess aligns with the Greek moon goddess Selene, the full-moon face of the triad.
The Wiccan quarter-guardians inherit the 'Watchtower' terminology from the Enochian Great Table via the Golden Dawn, while functioning as distinct elemental guardians.
